Now the barrier is not a refusal to retreat but a shut door. His father would need to notice the practical condition of compliance instead of treating the report of broken loose as the whole event.

n_4c909ed7.title: A slow pace can still exhaust the one being driven
n_4c909ed7.text: The father's giant soles return me to the manager's assured boots, but now the unequal cost of movement is explicit. One paternal step demands many movements from Gregor, until breath and attention fail. Calling it not quite a chase because it is slow makes me feel the danger of judging pressure by the stronger person's pace.

n_e4791386.title: The mother who needed protection moves to protect him
n_e4791386.text: The woman feared near death now runs, trips in loosened clothes and pleads for his life. I cannot leave her fixed in the role of fragile person kept away for her own good. Her bodily vulnerability remains visible in the same action as her courage. Embracing the father here carries a plea to stop, not proof of agreement with what he has done.

n_388b75cd.title: The father's new bearing changes capacity, not the fact of harm
n_388b75cd.text: I had kept Gregor's picture of his exhausted father separate from a settled verdict on what he could do. The upright uniformed man now makes that caution matter: the old picture was incomplete or conditions have changed. I do not yet know the cost of this apparent renewal. I do know he fills his pockets and throws until an apple drives into Gregor's back; uncertainty about work or motives cannot blur that act.

n_606e057f.title: A month passes around the apple that remains
n_606e057f.text: The time jump is abrupt, yet the apple stays physically in his flesh. I find that contrast more disturbing than a continuous account of every painful day: a whole month can pass without anyone venturing to remove it. Calling it a reminder gives it meaning, but I cannot let the meaning displace the untreated wound.

n_0fdd24e4.title: Nothing else narrows the promise of belonging
n_0fdd24e4.text: For a moment being remembered as family sounds like a turn toward care. Then the repetition of endure, closed down by nothing else, makes that promise contract. The sentence gives me both a limit on treating him as an enemy and a bleakly small account of what he can expect instead. I should not flatten that difference, but neither can I hear it as repair.

n_a66fb6a2.title: What stands between enduring him and tending the wound?
n_a66fb6a2.text: No one ventures to remove the apple. I do not know whether fear, lack of skill, aversion or some mixture keeps treatment away, nor whether removal would be safe. But leaving it is also an action with a cost: over a month of suffering. What would let someone seek help without pretending either intervention or delay harmless?

n_b957283a.title: Shared earning has arrived without easy adjustment
n_b957283a.text: The mother sews for a shop and Grete works in sales while studying for something better. That gives my gradual-redistribution guess real evidence, but the tired smiles and sleeping father prevent me from calling the adjustment manageable or care protected. The narrower fear that only one new person must carry all earning is not what I see; the strain may instead spread across them.

n_ed3d7ba6.title: Maybe learning can buy them more time later
n_ed3d7ba6.text: Maybe Grete's French and stenography will open a better job and give the household breathing room. I would look for improved terms or time, not assume that acquiring a skill automatically produces opportunity.

n_a7bc119a.title: Maybe earning and study will crowd out the remaining care
n_a7bc119a.text: Or exhaustion may leave less attention for Gregor even while more people contribute money. I would look for changes in food, cleaning or willingness to stay with him. Shared earning alone cannot tell me whether the rest of life remains livable.

n_06073d96.title: The opened door measures a hunger that injury cannot settle
n_06073d96.text: He watches one or two hours before the door opens and calls the sight of the family full compensation for lost movement. I hear how intensely he needs permitted company. Maybe satisfaction is sincere; maybe a tiny opening has become precious because so much contact has gone. I should not declare him secretly unhappy, but neither can his gratitude make the wound an acceptable price.

n_dcefedc4.title: The family he can see is not the evening he remembers
n_dcefedc4.text: He once longed for animated home life from damp hotel beds. Now he can watch home, but tired sewing, study and sleep fill the place where he remembers conversation. I feel a double distance: the door has opened, yet the life he hoped to rejoin has changed too. Their tired smiles leave a small sign of mutual warmth without proving that anyone has enough rest.

n_a669b23d.title: The uniform's readiness does not establish unlimited strength
n_a669b23d.text: The same uniform that made him look renewed now stays on through dirty, uncomfortable sleep, as though he awaits a superior's call. I no longer have to imagine work as a simple restoration of strength. His exhaustion is visible, even if I cannot tell how much of the bedtime resistance comes from fatigue, stubbornness or attachment to the role.

n_c7863ad1.title: Receiving help is not the same as having no agency
n_c7863ad1.text: He resists rising until the women lift him, then walks by himself and still draws more help after him. I cannot infer that all his difficulty is feigned, but I also cannot call the entire ritual unavoidable need. The women interrupt their own work repeatedly. Their care and his exhaustion deserve attention alongside the choices that make that care more demanding.

n_0af35cc2.title: Readiness for work can invade the work of resting
n_0af35cc2.text: He keeps the uniform as if awaiting his superior, yet needs a long family effort to reach the bed that would prepare him for six o'clock service. I see a loop: performing readiness may interfere with the rest readiness needs. The polished buttons on stained clothes make the loop almost absurdly visible. It is a possible account of the ritual, not proof that I know why he refuses the gown.

n_a216cf40.title: A closed door can shelter grief while deepening loneliness
n_a216cf40.text: After tending the father, the women sit cheek to cheek and ask for the door shut. I can imagine they need relief from being watched and room to cry or stare without another demand. At the same time Gregor's wound hurts again when he is put back in darkness. A boundary that protects their exhausted intimacy can wound his need for company without either experience cancelling the other.

n_dfe502b7.title: Hopelessness may turn a possible task into an impossible future
n_dfe502b7.text: They say moving is impossible because of him; he imagines a ventilated box and locates the deeper obstacle in hopelessness. Maybe the transport problem has become a container for a larger inability to imagine change. But knowing a box could move him is not knowing how to afford, organize and endure a move. Their exhausted state belongs in any account of what is possible.

n_ae256835.title: The ledger ends with two faces together
n_ae256835.text: The jewellery is first remembered as something worn with joy, then reported by sale price. I feel the household shrinking in possible occasions as well as money. Ending the same paragraph with the women cheek to cheek gives back a form of closeness that cannot be priced, even while Gregor is excluded from it. The opening who has time question becomes more painful when I see precisely whose time and pleasures have been used up.

n_2f9e3c73.title: Care has deteriorated in observable ways
n_2f9e3c73.text: The hurried food, unchecked leftovers and accumulating dirt give evidence beyond a general impression of tiredness. My earlier concern about earning crowding out care now has the predicted signs. Gregor's inability to name an appetizing food complicates feeding, but it does not explain away the disappearance of checking what he needs.

n_4730b51c.title: Exclusive responsibility persists after responsive care fades
n_4730b51c.text: Grete notices the dirt and still leaves it, yet resents another person cleaning. That strengthens the concern that being the responsible one can become distinct from attending to Gregor. It does not prove the earlier conjecture that she wanted a terrifying room. Exhaustion, touchiness and ownership of the role may overlap; I should test the pattern without claiming access to all her motives.

n_56e7a876.title: More cleaning is not automatically better care
n_56e7a876.text: The mother's major cleanup sounds like the obvious answer to dirt until the dampness makes him sick. I cannot choose a good caregiver simply by contrasting effort with neglect. What helps this particular body still has to be learned; the family argument then shifts attention from that result to who was allowed to act.

n_0ca9c74c.title: What he deserves is no longer measured by appetite
n_0ca9c74c.text: Earlier he would rather starve than ask Grete; now he imagines taking what he deserves even though he is not hungry. I hear a claim to consideration returning through anger. That anger does not tell him what food could help, but lack of appetite cannot make his demand for responsive care disappear.

n_58665292.title: He wants a say in what the door lets through
n_58665292.text: He once guarded his own closed door, then longed for visitors and watched for the evening opening. Now he hisses because nobody shuts out the quarrel. These changes make more sense to me as a wish for some control over contact than as inconsistent hunger for company. Seeing the family is not always the same experience; the open door can bring commotion as well as belonging.

n_bed0baf0.title: Lack of horror is not yet attentive care
n_bed0baf0.text: Before, fear seemed a major barrier to approaching him. Now a woman can look and address him calmly, but the new contact still fails to clean the room or respect his wish to be left alone. I have to separate fearlessness from care: willingness to approach supplies a capacity, not a settled purpose or a receptive relationship.

n_2a554ca4.title: The protected-care branch has failed in the present arrangement
n_2a554ca4.text: I had imagined shared work preserving manageable time for care. Grete is now explicitly exhausted and tired of caring as before, and the available cleaning woman brings disturbance rather than a reliable replacement. Shared earning occurred, but the protected-care part of that hopeful arrangement did not. This leaves future improvement possible without keeping the original expectation untouched.

n_81be97bb.title: New contact leaves old motives and future opportunity open
n_81be97bb.text: I still do not know what the sheet meant to Grete, why the picture first appealed to him, or what prevents treatment of the wound. Grete's study has not yet produced a reported better position, and I cannot attribute the burden arrangement to a proven policy about the reserve. The cleaning woman's direct words also do not settle whether Grete herself will address him receptively. I keep these mysteries rather than manufacture closure.

n_1763b6cd.title: A comic greeting ends with furniture held as a threat
n_1763b6cd.text: The repeated old dung beetle sounds almost jauntily familiar, but Gregor does not answer and wishes for useful cleaning instead. Then her open mouth and lifted chair make the scene grotesquely comic and dangerous at once. I find that tonal swing effective: a room's ordinary furniture becomes a possible blow to the back I know is wounded. His slow threatening turn matters too; the chair is raised in response, not thrown in this encounter.

n_070c485d.title: The tidy household has a room where its disorder goes
n_070c485d.text: The lodgers' meticulous order sounds comprehensive until every surplus object, even ash and kitchen garbage, arrives in his room. I find the reversal sharply bitter: the room earlier cleared for movement now absorbs the cost of order elsewhere. The glimpse of an object and a throwing hand makes the transfer feel stripped of any encounter with the person living there.

n_6b0e4042.title: Growing pleasure ends in hours of immobility
n_6b0e4042.text: He first pushes through the things because he has to, then with pleasure. I am glad the prose leaves him an activity that is not only misery, but its ending refuses an easy recovery: he becomes wretched and cannot move for hours. The small play with food, held and spat out, has a similar unease. Calling something a game does not make it nourishment or make the effort harmless.

n_0c05b3b7.title: Accepting the room has not restored eating
n_0c05b3b7.text: He first thinks sadness about the room explains the appetite, then becomes reconciled to the changes while food still stays in his mouth and is spat out. That weakens sadness as a sufficient explanation. The wound, changed body, food, isolation or some combination might matter, but I do not know. His adaptation to the clutter cannot certify that he is being nourished or that the conditions are acceptable.

n_389c6c96.title: Maybe appetite remains without a usable meal
n_389c6c96.text: He says he really has an appetite but not for these things. Maybe the near-refusal of food has been a mismatch between need and what is offered, not an absence of hunger. The chewing teeth make the mismatch feel bodily. I would need evidence of what he could actually take and keep before calling a different menu the answer.

n_67a2a6a8.title: Maybe this hunger also reaches beyond food
n_67a2a6a8.text: Or his hunger may include something this silent meal cannot supply: contact, purpose, a place among people. He has stopped using the open door on many nights, and now hears consumption where he once hoped for family life. That reading might coexist with literal need; it must not turn a starving body into a metaphor I no longer have to care about.

n_37500078.title: The authority to approve has moved into the family dining room
n_37500078.text: The central lodger tests the meat while mother and sister wait for permission to breathe easily; the father bows and the family eats elsewhere. I remember the boss's high desk, where another person's position organized Gregor's extra effort. The new hierarchy is domestic and financial, but I do not yet know its agreed terms. What I can see is the family's old place at the table occupied by people whose satisfaction they anxiously serve.

n_893ec800.title: Permission to hear her is not her expressed wish to perform
n_893ec800.text: The lodgers invite the young woman, and her father agrees as if he were playing. She prepares calmly, so I cannot call this resistance or coercion. But I also have not heard her say whether the recital is pleasure, obligation or both. The parents' exaggerated politeness is now explained by inexperience with renting; I should not silently turn all their deference into a contractual necessity.

n_73258e14.title: Indifference has not extinguished response
n_73258e14.text: The narration calls him indifferent to everything as he stops cleaning himself, but the playing draws him out. I should not let that broad phrase make his responsiveness disappear. Nor does approaching prove recovery or considerate judgment: the floor is spotless and the dirt on him comes from a neglected room. I see a live attraction within depletion, not a complete diagnosis of what he feels.

n_3e72e66a.title: The dirt carried outside has a history inside
n_3e72e66a.text: The careful list of threads, hair and food remnants makes his approach painfully visible against the spotless floor. I feel the risk of seeing him as the thing that dirties a clean household, but I remember where its unwanted things went. The music brings that hidden history across the threshold on his body. He has stopped scouring himself too; the image holds his depleted self-care and the room's neglect together rather than assigning every trace to one cause.

n_58f9e1aa.title: The recital opens a future only one person has spoken
n_58f9e1aa.text: A head inching along the floor becomes a whole imagined room: dress tugged, doors guarded, revelation, tears, a kiss. I feel how vividly the passage supplies the closeness he cannot obtain. But the fluent future contains no interruption from Grete. The beauty of the fantasy cannot make its voluntary ending something she has chosen.

n_33ca2a9d.title: No one values it arrives beside attentive parents
n_33ca2a9d.text: The family is caught up in the playing, yet he imagines taking Grete away because no one values it as he does. I hear a particular claim of depth turning into a claim of exclusivity. The lodgers' withdrawal and smoke are also read as disappointment, not given in a candid statement from them. I can share his captivation without treating his entire audience judgment as neutral description.

n_e822f28f.title: Music gives the broader hunger a concrete object
n_e822f28f.text: The thought of unknown nourishment now appears as the playing captivates him. That supports my guess that hunger reaches beyond the meal, while leaving actual undernourishment untouched. His question about being a beast also shows what appreciation means to his self-understanding; I do not want beauty to become another test he must pass to deserve care.

n_7840c105.title: Maybe the approach can bring a moment of recognition
n_7840c105.text: Maybe Grete will notice his attention and understand that the music reaches him. I would look for her approaching or responding to him as a listener, without assuming she would then want permanent life in his room.

n_dfe4a9dd.title: Maybe visibility will interrupt the music before recognition
n_dfe4a9dd.text: Or the others may notice his body before Grete can read the attraction behind his approach. I would look for alarm, the playing stopping, or renewed demands to withdraw. The dirt and the lodgers' anxious place in the room give that branch grounds, but not certainty.

n_e99cd3b7.title: Managing an expected alarm can create another source of it
n_e99cd3b7.text: The lodgers initially seem amused rather than frightened. The father rushes to conceal Gregor and push them back, and irritation follows. Maybe discovery of the hidden neighbor is part of their anger; maybe being managed so forcefully is. I see an attempt to control a feared reaction becoming part of the reaction's cause, without knowing how much weight each cause has.

n_83d64a22.title: The unfinished musician becomes the practiced bed-maker
n_83d64a22.text: Grete holds the violin as if still playing after the sound stops, then suddenly arranges the lodgers' beds with practiced speed. I feel a moment of disorientation giving way to a role she knows how to perform. That competence does not tell me her loss is small. The mother receives the instrument while struggling to breathe; neither woman becomes mere background because the dispute is loud.

n_ec849eac.title: The rental arrangement now carries a threatened loss
n_ec849eac.text: Before, I saw lodgers as an added income source whose standards displaced the family's space. Now they demand immediate departure without paying even for past days and threaten action. That is a serious new insecurity, not proof of a lawful entitlement or a loss already collected. Their emphatic certainty reminds me to keep a demand separate from an established right.

n_dde8fd77.title: A limit on sacrifice becomes a denial of belonging
n_dde8fd77.text: I can take seriously that Grete cannot keep living this way. Her work and the family's exhaustion are real. But refusing his name and calling him a monster goes beyond naming a limit: it removes him from the relation through which duty was last being remembered. Their need for a livable future does not make his felt life disappear, even if no easy arrangement protects everyone.

n_3a004166.title: Care's costs do not establish complete innocence
n_3a004166.text: She wants the family beyond criticism because they have tried everything humanly possible. I remember genuine care, but also unchecked food, dirt and the apple left in his back. Exhausted capacity might explain some failures; it does not make them disappear. I want to distinguish asking for help or an end to an unsustainable role from declaring every past action morally settled.

n_2ae7d142.title: A fallen violin gives way to a struck table
n_2ae7d142.text: The mother drops the violin and it resonates; then Grete strikes the table to introduce her verdict. I find that change of sound devastating: the music that opened a desired future becomes a broken-off tone before another voice closes down his name. Meanwhile I still know his disappointment, weakness and fear. The speech cannot make the inside of him vanish for me just by substituting monster.

n_6a8a4838.title: Maybe not knowing how will create a pause in action
n_6a8a4838.text: The father asks what to do and Grete can only shrug. Maybe that practical uncertainty will interrupt the momentum of her demand and leave time for some other arrangement or a fuller hearing. I would look for an actual delay or reconsideration, not mistake her tears for a withdrawal of the demand.

n_e561464e.title: Maybe exhaustion will make an undefined demand more dangerous
n_e561464e.text: Or their shared sense that they cannot endure more could lead to acting without examining a method or its costs. The mother cannot listen through coughing while the father agrees and Grete cries that this is killing them. I would look for whose voice is included before a decision, especially the mother who has protected him and the person being discussed.

n_d2fe1a90.title: A feared future is not proof of a single cause
n_d2fe1a90.text: Grete says she sees their deaths coming because of him. I can see her mother's coughing and the family's overwork, so the fear is not empty. But the work, sleeplessness, money dispute and recent confrontation are several pressures, and I have no evidence that removing Gregor would by itself restore either parent. Her forecast deserves a hearing without becoming a diagnosis or an established cure.

n_da7855e5.title: A place in the compromise depends on a disputed capacity
n_da7855e5.text: The father can imagine compromise if Gregor understands, and then accepts Grete's conviction that he does not. I see the value in treating someone as a participant rather than just managing him. But their inability to hear an answer has become a verdict on his capacity to receive one. Even if he could not negotiate, his experience would still create reasons for care; comprehension should change the way they engage him, not decide whether he counts.

n_73b7c22f.title: A question about understanding becomes borrowed certainty
n_73b7c22f.text: Before, perplexity left open a fuller hearing. Now the father briefly names compromise, then accepts Grete's conviction that he cannot understand, without attempting a new exchange. I know from his listening that comprehension exists, but I must not give the father my privileged access. The failure is the untested leap from not receiving an answer to being certain there can be none; the hopeful pause has produced a named possibility, not actual participation.

n_c88919f9.title: The remembered brother is made from the required departure
n_c88919f9.text: If it were Gregor, he would leave: the speech turns a test of conduct into a test of identity. I hear his old consideration being recruited against his present need to stay. The promised honored memory sounds tender, yet it makes affection easier once the person needing care is absent. The claim of an obvious plan to seize the apartment then makes a feared future feel like an observed intention.

n_e8c64f23.title: Maybe withdrawal can still contradict the takeover story
n_e8c64f23.text: If he moves back toward his own room, perhaps that visible direction could weaken the claim that he wants the whole apartment. I would look for anyone noticing retreat as retreat, rather than assume their fear cannot be corrected.

n_87d3f9ef.title: Maybe the threatening story will absorb even a retreat
n_87d3f9ef.text: Or once staying proves he is not Gregor and movement means starting up again, he may have no bodily signal they can receive as harmless. I would look for fear persisting despite withdrawal, or his absence being treated as the only acceptable answer. The father's response to her alarm makes that branch plausible, not inevitable.

n_3d1c36b7.title: A harmless intention can be seen without a place being restored
n_3d1c36b7.text: He wants to spare his sister and returns toward his room, striking his head as he turns. The fear passes and they watch sorrowfully. I can value that small correction: his intention seems to reach them. But recognition of harmlessness is not agreement that he belongs or an offer to ease the painful movement. I want neither to erase the change nor demand that he prove consideration through injury.

n_a4ce566f.title: His long return ends in her sudden finally
n_a4ce566f.text: The distance feels enormous to him now, though music had carried him across it almost unnoticed. The prose lets effort take time: puffing, rests, a stiff turn to look back. Then Grete springs and locks him in before he hears her coming. I feel two incompatible clocks in finally—her wait for enclosure and his exhausting journey to it.

n_6d8469d2.title: Maybe the closed room can at least allow rest
n_6d8469d2.text: He has completed a difficult return without being hurried. Maybe being out of the confrontation will let him stop spending the strength movement requires and recover some capacity. I would look for rest followed by easier movement or renewed interest, rather than assume the lock itself supplies care.

n_6ec7d8be.title: Maybe enclosure will hide a need that cannot wait
n_6ec7d8be.text: Or the quick bolt and finally may mean the household has withdrawn attention just when hunger and injury leave him least able to ask. I would look for whether anyone checks on his condition or whether being quiet is simply taken as the problem resolved. The danger is not proof of what anyone intends.

n_ae582d3e.title: Less pain was not recovery
n_ae582d3e.text: He feels pain weakening and relative contentment while he can no longer move. Then he dies. I have to give up the hope that rest here restores capacity; a quieter report of pain did not mean the danger was passing. The rotten apple and inflammation remain present, but I cannot isolate one medical cause from the whole history of injury, hunger and weakness.

n_40c83624.title: Accepting disappearance is not the same as willing the last breath
n_40c83624.text: He believes even more firmly than Grete that he must disappear and remembers the family lovingly. I need to hold those feelings without calling the death a freely chosen gift. His head sinks without his willing it. The peace is an experience to respect, not proof that the demand which preceded it was right or that he caused his own bodily ending.

n_dd2d24fd.title: The unanswered care question has lost its future for him
n_dd2d24fd.text: I have to abandon expecting a later treatment or shared conversation to repair his condition: his last breath has ended those possibilities for him. The questions about what prevented help and what earlier gestures meant remain unanswered, not disproved. Their persistence now records a cost of waiting for knowledge that never reached action, while I still cannot claim a particular intervention would have saved him.

n_62a8a082.title: Full understanding can still be mistaken for chosen refusal
n_62a8a082.text: The cleaner grants him complete understanding and thinks the stillness is an offended performance. I remember the imagined doctor who could call incapacity laziness. The mistake has changed its setting, not its form: an interpretation of intention arrives before attention to what the body can do. The family's denial of comprehension was no solution, but its opposite alone was not care either.

n_2415e205.title: They can see the thinness when he can no longer need food
n_2415e205.text: Grete remembers meals returning unchanged and now sees how thin he was. The information was not wholly absent; its bodily meaning becomes clear only when he is flat and still. I am struck by that delay without knowing how consciously she had held the earlier evidence. Noticing suffering afterward cannot repair it, but it changes the story that their care had left nothing unconsidered.

n_928f09e3.title: The first recorded check arrives too late for the enclosed person
n_928f09e3.text: The cleaner finds him dead in the morning and initially sees nothing unusual. That supports the feared branch that enclosure can hide a need until a response cannot help him. I should not add an unrecorded deliberate decision to let him die; what I have is a night ending in death and recognition arriving afterward.

n_86122cc0.title: Maybe relief is only one part of the surviving response
n_86122cc0.text: The father gives thanks, but the mother almost restrains the broom and Grete keeps looking at the body, apparently sleepless. Maybe relief exists with grief, guilt or exhausted attachment; I cannot decide those feelings from the gestures. I would look for how they treat his memory and each other afterward rather than let one declaration stand for every inner life.

n_e4c3ebff.title: Relief and grief now have room in the same response
n_e4c3ebff.text: The mother's melancholy smile, Grete's backward look and their tear-stained return support the possibility that thanks was not their only feeling. I can now name visible grief beside relief more confidently. I still do not know how they understand their part in his suffering or what their remembering will become; tears do not tell me every belief behind them.

n_f2b42f4a.title: Their joined posture changes who waits for permission
n_f2b42f4a.text: The lodgers step out expecting service as before, but the father approaches with wife and daughter still on his arms and insists they leave. I wonder whether acting as a joined family gives him confidence he lacked in the anxious pushing earlier. The central man recalculates and goes. This makes the previous deference look changeable; it does not prove that Gregor had to die before a boundary could be set, or settle the disputed payment.

n_b930fd90.title: Three letters make room for a need to rest
n_b930fd90.text: All three decide they need a day away and write to the people expecting their work. I hear something different from Gregor's early fear that one absence would make him suspect: rest is now named as earned and necessary. Their need deserves recognition in its own right. I cannot use that recognition to conclude he had to be lost before any of them could stop working for a day.

n_09fb0372.title: Refusing the details does not tell me the whole feeling
n_09fb0372.text: Rubbish is the cleaner's word, offered with a smile as a completed task. Mother and daughter bend over the letters and the father stops the account. I cannot make their silence prove either that they share the word or that they are honoring him. Grief, disgust, avoidance and a wish for privacy could overlap. I can see a real refusal to hear more and the cleaner's wounded pride without claiming their interiors settled.

n_c9d24cb2.title: The new prospects may be newly shared rather than newly created
n_c9d24cb2.text: They had not really questioned one another about their work and now discover favorable positions and prospects. Maybe part of the change is a shared picture becoming available, not simply external life becoming good after Gregor's death. The exhaustion I saw remains real. So does the evidence of opportunity now. Grete's earlier study has not been shown producing a new job, but I can no longer leave her future inside an account of pure narrowing.

n_0f4acb53.title: Setting the past aside still returns attention to the father
n_0f4acb53.text: The women stand embracing at the window; he calls them back, asks to set old matters aside and requests consideration for himself. I see a family trying to regain closeness, but also the familiar pull toward meeting his need first. I cannot know whether moving on will include remembering or suppress it. Their quick caresses establish affection, not that every person's grief has finished at the same time.

n_cf8fc8e1.title: Her stretching body exceeds the future imagined for her
n_cf8fc8e1.text: Grete grows animated and stretches in the sun; I want that vitality to count without treating her only as a replacement future for the family. Her parents read it as confirmation that they should find a husband. I remember the unspoken Conservatory plan: affection can again imagine a life for her before she has answered. The ending gives me hopeful movement and an unanswered question of agency, not proof that a marriage would help or harm her.
